prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a polished realistic product mockup board for an original mobile strategy puzzle game for AGES 9–12, titled exactly "RESCUE GRID". Entire canvas landscape. Restrained cool ivory background, small bold editorial title at top "RESCUE GRID", subtitle "Plan the route. Power the rescue.", small bottom label "STRATEGY PUZZLE • AGES 9–12".
Show one large realistic thin black-bezel landscape iPad on left and one realistic thin black-bezel portrait iPhone right, both complete front-on, subtle studio shadows, dominant crisp screen content. High fidelity shippable game UI with original stylish isometric low-poly 3D art like a premium indie strategy game. NOT preschool, no smiling vehicles, no baby animals, no nursery bubble buttons. Sharp friendly graphic design, deep navy UI, coral emergency vehicles, mint energy accents, seafoam water, cream urban blocks.
GAMEPLAY: player commands a small electric rescue rover across a flooded island town to deliver supplies to a rooftop rescue point. The landscape tablet screen has coherent compact isometric road-grid island map on left 75% with coral base lower left, connected streets, two labeled destinations A and B, flooded road blocked by water, a broken bridge crossing a channel, small repair drone hovering nearby. A cyan planned route runs from base along connected streets to bridge. Upper HUD "MISSION 04", "SUPPLIES 1/2", battery icon "ENERGY 8". Right sidebar contains task "Repair the bridge", a large illustrated repair card labeled "Repair • 2 energy", secondary task card "Deliver supplies", and primary bold coral button "DISPATCH" at bottom. Bottom map toolbar has undo and route icons. One clear strategic decision rather than random decorative counters. No active countdown, no frightening injury.
The portrait phone uses same art and same mission, with top mission/battery HUD, zoomed scrollable map in middle including bridge and A/B markers, a bottom sheet showing "Repair • 2 energy" and wide "DISPATCH" button, thumb-accessible undo. It reflows the task sidebar beneath the map. Large touch areas, readable type, clear controls and safe spacing around camera cutout. One cyan route and one blocked road immediately understandable.
No ads, shops, coins, microtransactions, chat, generic dashboards or surrounding decorative props. Both devices must depict plausible playable screens with refined UI, strong silhouette shapes, original art. This is an older-kids game design presentation, not a small-child learning app. Landscape canvas.

Use case: ui-mockup. Create a realistic high fidelity product mockup board for an original cozy ecosystem strategy game for AGES 9–12 called exactly "WILD POCKET". Landscape presentation on misty pale sage background. Upper editorial title "WILD POCKET", smaller subtitle "Restore an island. Balance its wild life.", small footer "ECOSYSTEM BUILDER • AGES 9–12".
Large front-facing realistic thin-black-bezel landscape iPad left and complete portrait iPhone right with subtle studio shadows, devices dominate canvas, crisp readable screens. Sophisticated original hand-painted isometric game art with a tactile papercraft feel, botanical greens, amber sunlight, ink-blue water, tiny expressive but naturally proportioned foxes, frogs and butterflies. Premium indie game mood for tweens, NOT baby cartoon, NOT preschool matching shapes or smiling frogs. No real game logos.
ACTUAL GAME: a small hex-tile island restoration puzzle in a floating sea. Tablet scene contains coherent connected hex tiles: woodland at left, meadow center, pond and reeds at right, a few barren hexes at lower edge, tiny fox beside woodland, butterflies over flowering meadow, frog by pond. ONE selected meadow tile has a fine white hex outline and a subtle link connecting its flowers to a butterfly icon. A left mini objective card reads "Restore the wetland", with two concise check rows "Connect pond + reeds" and "Shelter for 3 species". Upper HUD shows "DAY 04", water drop icon "6", leaf icon "8". Right compact inspector card reads "WILDFLOWERS" with icon benefit "Feeds pollinators" and cost "2 water". At bottom three chunky placement cards "Reeds", "Wildflowers", "Log shelter", with distinct painted item icons. Lower right large dark-forest button "PREVIEW DAY". UI feels clean, strategic, approachable, type fits.
Phone shows SAME island mission reflowed in portrait: top "DAY 04" resource strip, zoomed island in center, compact "Restore the wetland" objective pill, selected wildflower card with "2 water" lower down, a horizontal row of 3 placement cards and bottom "PREVIEW DAY". The island is recognizably the same shape, not cropped randomly. Large hit targets and adequate safe area around cutout.
No ads, timers, shop currencies, chat, school quiz styling or overwhelming statistical dashboards. Factual-looking ecology illustration but resource numbers are visibly game abstractions. Authentic achievable gameplay layout with refined 2D art and readable functional UI, not just scenery. Landscape canvas.

Use case: ui-mockup. Create a realistic polished product mockup board for an original cooking and experimentation game for AGES 9–12 called exactly "MONSTER FOOD TRUCK". Landscape presentation with muted warm cream background. Upper bold editorial title "MONSTER FOOD TRUCK", subtitle "Invent weird food. Win over weird customers.", bottom small label "CREATIVE COOKING • AGES 9–12".
One large realistic thin-black-bezel landscape iPad left and complete realistic portrait iPhone right, both front-on and fully visible, subtle product-photo shadows. Game screen occupies most of devices. Original vibrant stylish 2D indie cartoon art, crisp graphic silhouettes and subtle grain, quirky teenage monster customers in hoodies and caps, electric turquoise food-truck interior, plum purple shadows and coral cooking equipment. Funny cool tween vibe, NOT baby nursery monsters, NOT fluffy preschool puppets.
GAMEPLAY SCREEN on tablet: kitchen front cutaway. One lanky purple monster customer in yellow beanie leans into service window at upper middle, its illustrated order card reads "SPICY + CRUNCHY" with pepper and crispy-chip icons. Mid screen is a large preparation board holding a fantastical taco with black sesame shell, neon-orange sauce, green slaw and purple crunchy chips, rendered delicious and funny. Left panel "RECIPE LAB" has three clear illustrated method buttons "CHOP", "SIZZLE", "BLEND", with SIZZLE selected. Right compact panel "FLAVOR" shows two horizontal clearly labeled meters "HEAT" and "CRUNCH", each with an outlined target marker; heat fill nearly reaches target while crunch fill reaches target. Bottom ingredient tray has four distinct illustrated cards: pepper, slaw, crispy chips, glowing mushroom, each with a tiny meaningful flavor icon. Upper HUD reads "NIGHT MARKET" and "ORDER 2/5", NO ticking timer. Lower right large coral "SERVE" button and lower left undo. Strong obvious cooking interactions with ample space, not a crowded dashboard.
Phone shows same customer, same spicy crunchy order, same taco work area, same flavor meters, then a 2x2 ingredient tray and wide bottom "SERVE" button. Cooking methods as three small but tappable tabs above the work board. Layout intelligently reflows vertically, no miniaturized tablet sidebar. Consistent original monster design between screens.
No premium currencies, monetization, ads, chat, sharp dangerous realism, tiny unreadable paragraphs, copyrighted characters or decorative props around devices. This must look like a plausible attractive cooking game an 11-year-old would choose to play, with a real gameplay decision about ingredient properties. Landscape canvas.
